weekly_thesis: W36 made evidence authority the common interface between VLA policies, world models, maps, VLM judges, and runtime safety systems. The week began with metric geometry, horizon-aware VLA planning, executable world representations, and runtime alarms; it then sharpened into freshness-gated maps, typed action permissions, provenance-conserving fusion, feedback-matched world-model evaluation, and Friday's evidence-budgeted multimodal training and deployment papers. The weekly opportunity for APRL is to own a robot benchmark where every sensor, map update, generated future, compressed token set, and evaluator must prove that it changes action, recovery, privacy risk, or safety margin before it is allowed into the loop.

clusters.cluster: VLA authority moves from larger context to evidence-gated action permission
clusters.why_it_matters: The week repeatedly rejects the idea that a VLA should simply consume more prompts, memories, sensors, or demonstrations. Planning-horizon reasoning, typed motor programs, adaptive chunk stops, provenance-conserving action admission, evidence-gated modality regularization, real-to-sim behavior evaluation, and action-sufficient intermediate features all ask whether an input is authorized to change a command. APRL should therefore measure action delta, failure-warning lead time, and fallback timing before trusting context size or final success.
clusters.confidence: High - every weekday produced independent evidence around VLA action authority, stop contracts, provenance, evaluation, or modality gates.
clusters.lab_action: Run one shared manipulation suite with prompt authority, typed skill library, action chunk stop, provenance partition, modality relevance, real-to-sim judge, and intermediate structural supervision as independent conditions; compare action delta, unsafe permission, failure lead time, recovery success, and judge stability.

paper_autopsies.title: Sensing Which Modality Matters: Evidence-Gated Regularization for Robust VLA Policies
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Multimodal VLA policies often fuse every available sensor and hope training will ignore nuisance correlations.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract names modality entanglement: low-evidence sensors can still dominate under occlusion or distractors, while one informative sensor may not be sufficient.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A policy should become invariant to low-evidence sensors and sufficient on high-evidence sensors before multimodal fusion is trusted.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Turn sensor fusion into a per-frame, per-sensor evidence gate that regularizes the training objective without inference-time overhead.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: EGR derives task-relevance signals and applies state-conditional consistency objectives for low-evidence invariance and high-evidence sufficiency.

decisive_evidence.claim: The paper introduces a BEHAVIOR-1K diagnostic suite and 47 rollout-based skills for modality entanglement.
It reports gains under uninformative-sensor corruption, single-sensor fallback, and physical-object distractors on two real robot embodiments.
APRL should evaluate whether each sensor actually changes action safety before treating more modalities as stronger evidence.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If evidence gates collapse under unseen tasks or new sensor layouts, the method may be regularizing benchmark-specific correlations.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Create scenes where tactile, wrist, and external camera cues alternate between helpful, irrelevant, and misleading while task success is held constant.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Multimodal evidence is useful only after low-evidence invariance and high-evidence sufficiency are separated.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for multi-camera and visuotactile robot policies; weaker for single-sensor settings without an evidence partition.

paper_autopsies.title: Scal3R: Learning Efficient Multi-Relative Pose Query for Scalable Online 3D Reconstruction
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Online reconstruction often anchors pose regression to the first frame, forcing long videos into extrapolation beyond training distribution.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract says depth stays locally stable while the global pose head collapses, so pose and local geometry fail differently.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A reconstruction can be robot-usable only if global pose drift is repaired without discarding stable local depth evidence.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Reformulate online reconstruction as multi-reference relative pose querying with lightweight tokens and pose-graph loop closure.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: Scal3R injects learnable pose-query tokens into a frozen backbone and queries poses relative to multiple past keyframes.

decisive_evidence.claim: The paper reports more than 60 percent average ATE reduction on KITTI over the online baseline.
It uses online pose-graph optimization with loop closure to suppress long-range drift.
APRL should score feed-forward reconstruction by relocalization and route or grasp changes under accumulated pose error.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If drift reduction does not improve downstream localization or manipulation frames, Scal3R remains a reconstruction metric win rather than a robot-validity win.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Stress repeated corridors, moving objects, and loop-closure aliases where local depth appears stable but global action frames flip.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Separate local geometry evidence from global pose authority before releasing a map for robot action.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for long-video mapping and navigation; less direct for short tabletop clips where first-frame anchoring is not the bottleneck.

paper_autopsies.title: Do Better Imagined Rollouts Mean Better Robot Control? A Controlled Study of World-Model Evaluation Under Feedback
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Predictive models for robotics are often judged by open-loop rollout accuracy over a fixed horizon.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract shows that closed-loop robots act, receive measurements, update state, and recompute control, so rollout metrics can rank estimators differently.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A rollout benchmark is informative only if its prediction horizon and measurement-update schedule match the feedback pattern of deployment.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Evaluate predictive models across replay, measurement-free rollout, and closed-loop tracking under controlled sensing conditions.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: The study varies rollout horizon and measurement-update interval in a differential-drive path-tracking task with biased odometry and intermittent landmarks.

decisive_evidence.claim: Rollout error selects a different estimator from the closed-loop optimum in 18 of 24 sensing conditions.
Replay RMSE correlates more strongly with closed-loop cross-track RMSE than rollout error.
APRL should publish the correction schedule whenever using imagined rollouts to justify robot control.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If the same mismatch does not appear in richer manipulation or locomotion controllers, the result may be estimator-task specific.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Vary landmark dropouts, odometry bias, correction interval, and planning horizon while measuring closed-loop task ranking.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: A prediction horizon without a correction schedule is an incomplete robot metric.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for state-estimation and planning loops; less direct for fully reactive policies without explicit rollout evaluation.

paper_autopsies.title: Not All Agreement Counts as Corroboration: Provenance-Conserving Multi-View Fusion for Typed Action Admission in Human-Robot Collaboration
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Embodied systems can treat repeated agreement as stronger evidence even when all predictions came from the same observation.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract says predictive agreement alone does not determine whether evidence warrants action because evidential origin matters.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A robot should count support only across independent provenance units, then map unmet release conditions to hold, confirm, or fallback.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Treat evidence countability as a relational variable for action admission instead of a local confidence score.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: PACT retains support shared within each provenance unit and accumulates only across countable units under a supplied partition.

decisive_evidence.claim: Within-camera duplication leaves 720 typed responses per checkpoint unchanged.
Camera-grouped PACT admits 47 of 57 reference-consistent candidates with no observed reference-inconsistent admission in 60 episodes.
APRL should distinguish computational multiplicity from evidence multiplicity before authorizing actions.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If provenance partitions are unavailable or wrong, the release gate may reject useful evidence or admit correlated errors.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Duplicate one camera, create correlated occlusions, and swap provenance partitions while keeping predictions fixed.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Agreement is corroboration only when the sources are separately countable.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for multi-camera collaboration and typed action gates; less direct for single-sensor policies without provenance metadata.

paper_autopsies.title: FailBench: How Reliable are VLMs at Judging Robot Task Success?
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Robot pipelines increasingly use VLMs as inexpensive judges for manipulation outcomes.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract says existing benchmarks offer limited evidence of cross-domain generalization for robot failure detection.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A judge can authorize evaluation conclusions only if it detects failure modes across tasks, domains, and visual conditions.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Make robot-success judging itself a benchmarked perception problem rather than an assumed service.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: FailBench supplies manipulation outcome examples for testing whether VLMs can reliably judge task success and failure.

decisive_evidence.claim: The benchmark comprises 2,197 manipulation examples.
It targets cross-domain robot failure detection rather than ordinary VQA accuracy.
APRL should validate every VLM evaluator before using it to rank robot policies.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If the benchmark lacks force, tactile, or invisible-state failures, a VLM may pass while missing robot-relevant failures.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Create visually successful but physically invalid trials, and physically successful but visually ambiguous trials, then compare judge rankings.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Evaluation agents need their own deployment benchmark.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for vision-observable manipulation outcomes; incomplete for hidden contact, force, or proprioceptive failures.

paper_autopsies.title: Seeing Less Is Not Seeing Safely: Privacy Leakage from Task-Scoped Robot Perception Exports
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: A robot perception export can be treated as safe once raw sensor data stay local and only task-scoped structure leaves the device.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract says structured exports still leak household information through semantics, geometry, spatial structure, and task targets.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: A perception export should be released only after task utility and multiple residual inference risks are evaluated together.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Profile downstream robot representations by utility, direct exposure, and held-out representation-aware privacy attacks.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: TFPD keeps rich perception local and evaluates navigation, collision checking, and object-goal exports on AI2-THOR and ProcTHOR splits.

decisive_evidence.claim: Three navigation exports achieve identical success and path ratio while linkability ranges from 0.532 to 0.970.
Replacing explicit target labels with target regions reduces target-category macro-F1 while preserving near-identical task success.
APRL should evaluate robot representation exports as safety and privacy release decisions, not logging details.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If held-out attackers are weak or scene distributions are too narrow, leakage ordering may not transfer to real homes.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Test target, geometry, topological, and semantic exports against attackers trained on disjoint houses and tasks.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: Seeing less is not a safety proof unless task utility and residual inference risk are jointly bounded.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for domestic robots and cloud planner interfaces; less direct for fully local deployments with no representation export.

paper_autopsies.title: WISE: World-model-guided Imagination Scheduling for Efficient Post-training of Vision-Language-Action Models
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: World models are often used as always-on imagined rollout engines for policy refinement.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract says imagination value varies by execution stage, while long rollouts can accumulate errors and introduce unreliable supervision.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: Imagined futures should refine policy actions only at interaction-relevant states and inside a trusted horizon.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Schedule when and how world-model imagination is invoked during VLA post-training instead of using full imagination everywhere.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: WISE selectively invokes bounded multi-view rollouts, evaluates candidate futures with progress and completion signals, and uses relative outcomes for action refinement.

decisive_evidence.claim: The method reports consistent improvements across manipulation tasks while reducing GPU computation time by about 80 percent compared with full imagination.
Real-world evaluations show gains in robustness and generalization under distribution shifts.
APRL should record where imagination changes action ranking and where it becomes unreliable supervision.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If scheduling mostly removes hard cases, it may improve efficiency while leaving rare failure recovery unsolved.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Force imagination at contact transitions, ambiguous object states, and recovery branches to find the horizon where supervision turns harmful.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: World-model imagination is an intervention with timing and stop conditions.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Strong for manipulation VLA post-training; weaker for policies whose world model cannot represent contact or hidden state.

paper_autopsies.title: TRaIL-Odom: Tightly Coupled Continuous Time Radar-IMU-LiDAR Odometry with Adaptive Doppler Weighting
paper_autopsies.status_quo_belief: Radar-LiDAR fusion often applies fixed residual weights even when LiDAR geometry and radar Doppler are directionally informative in different ways.
paper_autopsies.friction: The abstract says fixed radar weighting misallocates Doppler information across translational directions under geometric degeneracy.
paper_autopsies.hidden_premise: Sensor fusion should allocate trust by the currently weak motion subspace, not by a global sensor prior.
paper_autopsies.conceptual_move: Treat Doppler constraints as direction- and scan-dependent evidence that is reweighted against LiDAR geometric anisotropy.
paper_autopsies.mechanism: TRaIL-Odom combines per-point Doppler reweighting with scan-wise radar gain scheduling in a tightly coupled continuous-time odometry framework.

decisive_evidence.claim: Across 13 sequences the method reports state-of-the-art overall performance and clear advantages in degenerate scenes.
In three degenerate ablations, both adaptive modules reduce RMSE ATE and RTE by 86.0 percent and 78.5 percent relative to fixed weighting.
APRL should condition odometry fusion weights on which direction is currently unobservable before planning trusts the pose.

paper_autopsies.falsification_frontier: If adaptive weights do not improve recovery in robot navigation decisions, the odometry gain may not translate beyond trajectory metrics.
paper_autopsies.adversarial_read: Use tunnels, flat walls, wet surfaces, and lateral motion where radar and LiDAR disagree about the weak direction.
paper_autopsies.transferable_thinking_tool: A sensor's evidence value is directional and state-dependent.
paper_autopsies.transfer_boundary: Direct for field robots with radar, LiDAR, and IMU; less direct for pure vision SLAM without Doppler constraints.

new: Friday adds a clear evidence-budget axis: sensors, tokens, privacy exports, and imagination steps must prove action relevance before use.
Robot privacy exports appear as an action-release concern rather than a logging or compliance side issue.
World-model scheduling and physical verification make imagination timing a first-class experimental variable.
strengthening: Action admission, provenance, and fallback permission strengthened across VLA, HRI, world models, and VLM judge papers.
Robot-usable geometry strengthened through metric perception, dynamic semantic maps, multi-view tracking, surgical reconstruction, pose repair, and radar-LiDAR odometry.
Efficiency work strengthened around decisive-cue retention rather than raw token, frame, or latency reduction.
commoditizing: Generic more-data VLA claims, pretty world-model rollouts, and pruning-only speedups look weak unless they expose which evidence variable changed action.
contradiction: The same week celebrates broader multimodal robot context and warns that extra context can be redundant, correlated, privacy-leaking, or unsafe without explicit evidence gates.
missing_axis: No single public benchmark yet combines modality relevance, robot-usable geometry, world-model feedback timing, VLM judge reliability, privacy leakage, and runtime safety margin in one closed-loop robot episode.

strategy_board.why_now: W36 produced repeated evidence gates across VLA, maps, world models, VLM judges, token pruning, privacy exports, and runtime monitors.
strategy_board.what_others_optimize: Most papers still optimize isolated success rate, reconstruction score, VQA accuracy, token count, or runtime false positives.
strategy_board.our_contrarian_bet: APRL should own the shared action-admission protocol that says when evidence is allowed to influence the robot.
strategy_board.required_moat: Synchronized robot episodes with sensor provenance, modality relevance, map drift, compressed evidence, privacy attack labels, safety margins, and fallback outcomes.

score_rationale.strategic_fit: Directly matches APRL robot perception, SLAM, VLA, and safety interests.
score_rationale.asymmetry: A small lab can win by owning hard evidence episodes rather than model scale.
score_rationale.timing: The evidence-gate vocabulary is emerging before standards settle.
score_rationale.tractability: A five-episode probe can be started with existing robots and cameras.
score_rationale.defensibility: Curated evidence partitions and failure labels become hard-to-copy assets.
score_rationale.scientific_depth: The question separates evidence authority from final success.

strategy_board.one_week_probe: Build five episodes with informative, irrelevant, duplicated, missing, and privacy-sensitive evidence sources.
strategy_board.four_week_build: Benchmark fusion, VLA, map, VLM judge, pruning, privacy export, and runtime-monitor variants on the same admission labels.
strategy_board.success_metric: Evidence gates change unsafe action permission or recovery timing before final success diverges on three failure families.
strategy_board.stop_condition: Stop if evidence partitions do not change decisions beyond ordinary confidence or terminal success.
strategy_board.paper_path: Evidence-budgeted action admission for multimodal robot intelligence.
strategy_board.asset_path: Robot episodes, synchronized evidence partitions, action deltas, fallback labels, privacy attacks, and safety margins.

strategy_board.why_now: The week tied metric geometry, dynamic maps, multi-view tracking, surgical reconstruction, pose repair, and radar-LiDAR odometry into one release-gate problem.
strategy_board.what_others_optimize: Reconstruction appearance, ATE, correspondence accuracy, or isolated map quality.
strategy_board.our_contrarian_bet: A map should be accepted only if its error predicts route, grasp, inspection, or safety outcomes under robot deployment conditions.
strategy_board.required_moat: Robot trajectories, weak-label maps, dynamic scenes, deformable wires, inspection targets, sensor degeneracy, and downstream action outcomes.

score_rationale.strategic_fit: Core APRL SLAM and robot perception work.
score_rationale.asymmetry: Deployment-validity episodes beat generic reconstruction scale.
score_rationale.timing: 3D foundation models, Gaussian maps, and sensor fusion are converging now.
score_rationale.tractability: A corridor and tabletop probe are feasible in one week.
score_rationale.defensibility: Repeated robot routes and task outcomes are reusable assets.
score_rationale.scientific_depth: Links representation error to action consequence.

strategy_board.one_week_probe: Record two route and tabletop scenes with pose aliases, moving objects, wire-like contacts, and weak semantic labels.
strategy_board.four_week_build: Compare reconstruction, SLAM, multi-view tracking, semantic maps, and radar-LiDAR odometry against downstream robot tasks.
strategy_board.success_metric: A robot-validity score predicts action failure better than ATE, PSNR, or segmentation mAP alone.
strategy_board.stop_condition: Stop if standard pose or segmentation error fully explains downstream failures.
strategy_board.paper_path: Operational geometry validity for robot maps and reconstruction.
strategy_board.asset_path: Robot route data, calibration, map states, object/contact annotations, drift labels, and downstream outcomes.

strategy_board.why_now: W36 repeatedly asks whether imagined futures are timed, verified, action-faithful, and risk-qualified.
strategy_board.what_others_optimize: Visual plausibility, rollout error, video reward, or policy gain in isolation.
strategy_board.our_contrarian_bet: A world model should be blocked from policy learning unless it preserves the action consequence under the actual feedback schedule.
strategy_board.required_moat: Counterfactual robot futures, measurement-update schedules, physical-obligation labels, risk memories, and policy-correction outcomes.

score_rationale.strategic_fit: Close to APRL robot execution, though model integration may be heavier.
score_rationale.asymmetry: A validity benchmark can expose failures in larger models.
score_rationale.timing: WAM and world-model evaluation criteria are still unsettled.
score_rationale.tractability: A small replay probe is easy; full WAM comparison is harder.
score_rationale.defensibility: Action-consequence traces and feedback schedules are reusable.
score_rationale.scientific_depth: Tests causal action state, not visual texture alone.

strategy_board.one_week_probe: Replay two manipulation and one navigation task with open-loop, intermittent-feedback, and scheduled-imagination variants.
strategy_board.four_week_build: Compare WAM, JEPA, reward-model, and physical-verifier gates by closed-loop action ranking and recovery outcome.
strategy_board.success_metric: Feedback-matched metrics predict robot control ranking better than ordinary visual or rollout scores.
strategy_board.stop_condition: Stop if all metrics rank methods identically once realistic feedback is included.
strategy_board.paper_path: Feedback-faithful evaluation for robot world-action models.
strategy_board.asset_path: Rollout traces, feedback schedules, counterfactual actions, physical failures, risk labels, and policy outcomes.
